# Background

In mouse microglia the surface lectin CD22 carries an ITIM motif in its cytoplasmic tail, and
phosphorylated ITIM motifs recruit the phosphatase SHP-1. Reported in this study: a blocking antibody
against CD22 raises the clearance of injected myelin debris by microglia; microglia carrying a CD22
point mutant in which the ITIM tyrosine is replaced by phenylalanine clear debris as well as
antibody-treated cells do; in a HEK293 reconstitution CD22 co-precipitates with SHP-1 only when the
ITIM tyrosine is intact; and surface CD22 levels on microglia are unchanged by the antibody.

# Question

What is the primary mechanism by which CD22 restrains microglial clearance of myelin debris, and
which entities does that mechanism turn on?
